tests.description: Every step is a REAL call against the bound catalog, so a step with no explanation would leave a viewer unable to tell what it demonstrated.
tests.key: DEMO_SEQUENCE › explains every step it runs

tests.description: read_brief comes BEFORE read_map: an agent handed a long document orients on its outline before deciding what to pull, and the scripted turn is the only place that ordering is written down.
tests.key: DEMO_SEQUENCE › orients on the brief before reading the map

tests.description: The turn has to end somewhere a person can act, and the slice is where WebMCP cannot bind — a preview has no live agent, so this scripted step is the only way the slice path is exercisable at all.
tests.key: DEMO_SEQUENCE › proposes a slice that names what it would settle

tests.description: The sequence is the closest thing here to a written description of one agent turn: say what you are about to do, read, add, ask, report back. Losing the ask would make it a demo of writes rather than an exchange.
tests.key: DEMO_SEQUENCE › walks a full turn including the question that waits on the person

tests.description: The plane is scaled, so screen travel has to be divided by the scale — without it a node drifts further from the pointer the further you zoom in.
tests.key: MapNodePill drag › converts screen travel into map pixels using the scale

tests.description: Below the threshold the gesture is a click, which is what keeps a label selectable and leaves room for click-to-ask on the same element.
tests.key: MapNodePill drag › does not report a nudge for movement under the threshold

tests.description: A read-only mount — an isolated scenario with no map to write back to — must not install a gesture at all.
tests.key: MapNodePill drag › is inert when no nudge handler is given

tests.description: The feedback complaint that produced this test: the node has to follow the pointer, so movement is reported on every move rather than only on release.
tests.key: MapNodePill drag › reports movement continuously while the drag is in flight

tests.description: The committed delta is what gets persisted, so it must be the total travel from where the drag began, not the last increment.
tests.key: MapNodePill drag › reports the total delta once on release

tests.description: The frame beneath pans on pointerdown, so a pointer that lands on a node must not also move the map.
tests.key: MapNodePill drag › stops the pointerdown from reaching the panning canvas

tests.description: Reaching for the fold control is not a drag of the node it sits on.
tests.key: MapNodePill fold affordance › does not start a node drag when the fold control is pressed

tests.description: Unfolded, the control says what it will do rather than what it is hiding.
tests.key: MapNodePill fold affordance › offers to fold a node that has descendants

tests.description: Folded, it reports the cost — the count is what tells you whether the branch is worth opening again.
tests.key: MapNodePill fold affordance › reports the hidden count once folded

tests.description: The pill is presentational: it reports which node was folded and leaves the decision about what that means to its caller.
tests.key: MapNodePill fold affordance › reports the toggle for its own node id

tests.description: No children means nothing to fold, so the control must not appear at all.
tests.key: MapNodePill fold affordance › shows no fold control for a node with nothing under it

tests.description: The kind has to be in the accepted set at all — this is what makes it wake an agent parked on await_user_activity rather than sitting inert.
tests.key: POST /api/maps/:id/exchange — user.question › accepts user.question as a user-writable kind

tests.description: Asking about a node must not change it. The person has not decided anything yet, so marking, reopening or reordering the node would be the route inventing an act they did not perform.
tests.key: POST /api/maps/:id/exchange — user.question › leaves the node it asks about untouched

tests.description: The ordinary case, and the reason the label is denormalised: the rail names the node, and it should not have to re-query per row to do it.
tests.key: POST /api/maps/:id/exchange — user.question › records the question with the node label resolved

tests.description: The check that matters. A node on somebody else's map must be refused, not logged here — otherwise the ownership boundary the route already keeps for the map itself has a hole in it at the payload.
tests.key: POST /api/maps/:id/exchange — user.question › refuses a node that belongs to a different map

tests.description: A question about a node that does not exist at all is the same refusal — there is nothing for it to be about.
tests.key: POST /api/maps/:id/exchange — user.question › refuses a nodeId that names nothing

tests.description: Without an id this is a note wearing a question's name, and the agent is back to guessing which pill was meant.
tests.key: POST /api/maps/:id/exchange — user.question › refuses a question with no nodeId

tests.description: Folding is a reading posture, so it has to be reversible in place.
tests.key: ThinkingMapView folding › brings the branch back when unfolded

tests.description: Folding one branch must not disturb another.
tests.key: ThinkingMapView folding › leaves other branches alone

tests.description: Folding filters the layout's INPUT, so the descendants genuinely leave the map — the behaviour that lets an oversized tree re-tidy and get narrower.
tests.key: ThinkingMapView folding › removes a folded branch’s descendants from the map

tests.description: The count is counted over the whole map rather than the visible slice, so it stays truthful once the branch it describes has gone.
tests.key: ThinkingMapView folding › reports how much a folded branch is holding

tests.description: A committed drag is written back to the map it belongs to, and it must NOT go through the exchange log — a move is arrangement, not thinking.
tests.key: ThinkingMapView nudges › persists a committed nudge to the positions endpoint

tests.description: An isolated scenario has no map to write back to; the map must still be draggable, the arrangement simply does not outlive the page.
tests.key: ThinkingMapView nudges › stays manipulable with no map id, without attempting a write

tests.description: Fit is disabled until there is something to reset, so a live button never leaves the person wondering what it did.
tests.key: ThinkingMapView viewport › disables fit until the viewport is the person’s

tests.description: Zoom is a ratio in both directions, so zooming out has to undo zooming in rather than bottoming out at the fit.
tests.key: ThinkingMapView viewport › lowers the scale when zoom out is pressed

tests.description: The controls promise something the map can do; an empty map can do none of it, so offering them would be a promise it cannot keep.
tests.key: ThinkingMapView viewport › offers no viewport controls on an empty map

tests.description: The counterpart to the empty case: with a tree on screen, all three controls have to be reachable.
tests.key: ThinkingMapView viewport › offers zoom and fit once there is a map to manipulate

tests.description: Zooming in has to raise the readout — this is the whole point of the control, and the readout is the only thing that says where the map is.
tests.key: ThinkingMapView viewport › raises the scale when zoom in is pressed

tests.description: The reset hands control back to the auto-fit rather than computing a scale of its own, which is what makes it exact instead of approximate.
tests.key: ThinkingMapView viewport › returns to the auto-fit scale when fit is pressed

tests.description: The regression this file exists for: WebMcpBridge renders copy promising these tools are reachable, so all seven must actually appear beside it.
tests.key: WebMcpBridge - NoAgent › renders every catalog tool rather than an empty list

tests.description: WebMcpBridge renders its resting state — the one every preview and capture shows. It must say an agent is absent, with a reason, rather than looking broken or, worse, claiming a connection it does not have.
tests.key: WebMcpBridge - NoAgent › reports that no agent is attached, with a reason

tests.description: With nothing outstanding, WebMcpBridge shows the trigger rather than the answer block, and displays a zero count.
tests.key: WebMcpBridge - NoAgent › shows nothing awaiting an answer

tests.description: Answering releases the agent, and WebMcpBridge renders its resting state again. The answer must reach the log too, since an agent that already gave up can only find it there.
tests.key: WebMcpBridge - pending states › clears the questions and records the answer once the person replies

tests.description: WebMcpBridge renders the none-to-some boundary: exactly one question outstanding, with its text on screen.
tests.key: WebMcpBridge - pending states › renders a single outstanding question

tests.description: WebMcpBridge displays both questions and shows the status flipped to working — the agent's turn is paused until the person answers.
tests.key: WebMcpBridge - pending states › renders both questions and marks the agent as working

tests.description: The many state: WebMcpBridge renders all five full-sentence questions rather than truncating to the first few.
tests.key: WebMcpBridge - pending states › renders every question when an agent asks several at once

tests.description: An answered call is a success, and its status is what an agent branches on.
tests.key: answeredResponse › marks the result answered and is not an error

tests.description: The agent needs both the question and the answer, since it may have asked several and cannot match them up from the answers alone.
tests.key: answeredResponse › reports each question with the answer it received

tests.description: Nothing is genuinely nothing.
tests.key: approxPages › counts an empty document as zero pages

tests.description: A short brief is still one page, never zero.
tests.key: approxPages › counts any non-empty document as at least one page

tests.description: A negative count is nonsense input; it must not produce a negative page.
tests.key: approxPages › never returns a negative page count

tests.description: Roughly 1,800 characters to the page, rounded.
tests.key: approxPages › scales with length

tests.description: The label has to change too. A send control reading "Ask the agent" with nothing attached is the exact overpromise this module exists to prevent.
tests.key: askPresence › drops the promise of a reply from the send label when nothing is attached

tests.description: With someone listening the control should say what it does — ask — rather than the neutral "send" that reads the same in both worlds.
tests.key: askPresence › names the agent in the send label when one is listening

tests.description: Guarding the negative directly: no branch may promise an answer from an agent that is not there.
tests.key: askPresence › never claims an agent will answer when none is attached

tests.description: Both branches must be usable copy — an empty string would render as a control with no label and a blank line where the honesty should be.
tests.key: askPresence › returns non-empty copy in both states

tests.description: The wake is the real mechanism and worth saying, because it is what makes asking different from leaving a note.
tests.key: askPresence › says asking wakes the agent when one is listening

tests.description: The whole point: absence is stated, not glossed over.
tests.key: askPresence › says plainly that no agent is attached when none is

tests.description: The two states must be distinguishable, or the UI is not actually telling the person which case they are in.
tests.key: askPresence › says something different in each state

tests.description: Several nodes asked about across a session all keep their marks.
tests.key: askedNodeIds › collects every distinct node across the log

tests.description: The ordinary case: the id travels in the payload, which is the whole reason this is its own kind rather than a note with a name in the prose.
tests.key: askedNodeIds › collects the node a question names

tests.description: A node asked about twice is still one marked node — the mark says whether, not how many.
tests.key: askedNodeIds › counts a node asked about twice only once

tests.description: Every other kind in the log must leave the marks alone — notes and answers carry node ids too, and marking those would badge half the map.
tests.key: askedNodeIds › ignores every other kind of event

tests.description: A map nobody has touched yet must produce no rows at all, so the rail can show its own explanation of how anything gets into it.
tests.key: askedNodeIds › is empty for an empty log

tests.description: A payload that lost its id must not throw and must not mark anything — one unattributable question should not take the marks off the rest.
tests.key: askedNodeIds › skips a question with a missing or non-string nodeId

tests.description: No agent at all — the common case, including every codeyam capture. It must be a silent no-op with a disposer that is safe to call.

tests.description: The pre-March-2026 convention the @mcp-b/global polyfill still ships: one call replaces the whole set, so disposal clears it with an empty set.

tests.description: A name left registered by a binding that failed to dispose must not take down the whole binding — losing one tool beats losing all seven.
tests.key: bindTools › keeps binding the rest when one registration throws

tests.description: The current spec convention (Chrome 146+): one registerTool per tool.
tests.key: bindTools › registers every tool through registerTool when that convention is present

tests.description: Disposal must remove exactly what was registered, or re-binding the same name on the next map throws InvalidStateError.
tests.key: bindTools › unregisters everything it registered when disposed

tests.description: The state the feature exists to make visible: work scheduled early that tests no assumption. It is reported, never filtered out.
tests.key: buildSequence › flags a slice that names no node at all

tests.description: Every other kind on a finished map — the idea, the next steps, the directions — belongs to a different region of the summary screen.
tests.key: buildSequence › ignores nodes that are not slices

tests.description: The sequence is numbered on screen and claims the first entry is the smallest thing worth building, so insertion order would misstate the plan.
tests.key: buildSequence › orders slices by order rather than input position

tests.description: A slice can outlive the assumption it was written for. That is reported as its own state rather than rendered as a blank line.
tests.key: buildSequence › reports a slice whose target has been deleted

tests.description: A slice may settle a risk or an open question just as legitimately as an assumption, so the link is not restricted by the target's kind.
tests.key: buildSequence › resolves a target of any kind, not just assumptions

tests.description: The ordinary path: a slice that names a live node reports what it settles.
tests.key: buildSequence › resolves the node a slice would settle

tests.description: A map that ended in next steps with no slices must render its hint rather than break, so the empty case is a value and not a special case.
tests.key: buildSequence › returns an empty sequence for a map with no slices

tests.description: A slice pointing at itself resolves to itself rather than looping or being treated as dangling — nothing here walks the link transitively.
tests.key: buildSequence › tolerates a slice that names itself

tests.description: Only the two read-only tools should carry annotations; attaching them everywhere would tell an agent a write is safe to retry speculatively.
tests.key: buildToolDescriptors › attaches annotations only to the tools that declare them

tests.description: Each descriptor must be wired to its OWN tool — a shared or misbound executor would silently run the wrong tool for every call.
tests.key: buildToolDescriptors › binds each descriptor to its own tool name

tests.description: The description and schema are how the agent decides whether and how to call a tool, so they must come from the catalog rather than be restated.
tests.key: buildToolDescriptors › carries each tool’s description and schema through

tests.description: What a browser agent gets registered. A tool missing from this set is a capability the agent silently does not have.
tests.key: buildToolDescriptors › describes every catalog tool

tests.description: The `+1` case, which is where an off-by-one in the walk would show first.
tests.key: collapsedDescendantCount › counts a single-child branch

tests.description: The count is the whole subtree, because that is what folding takes away.
tests.key: collapsedDescendantCount › counts every descendant, not just direct children

tests.description: The starting node is excluded from its own count, so the root reports six of the seven rows rather than all seven.
tests.key: collapsedDescendantCount › counts everything below the root

tests.description: Zero is what makes the fold affordance stay off a leaf.
tests.key: collapsedDescendantCount › is zero for a leaf

tests.description: A node deleted between render and count must read as zero rather than throwing under the pill that asked.
tests.key: collapsedDescendantCount › is zero for an id that is not on the map

tests.description: ...unless something actually cites it, in which case the citation is real and the section is genuinely accounted for.
tests.key: computeBriefCoverage › counts an empty section that something cites

tests.description: The base case: each section reports how many nodes cite it, and the list stays in document order so the panel can render it without re-sorting.
tests.key: computeBriefCoverage › counts the nodes citing each section, in document order

tests.description: An unreferenced node is the normal case — most nodes have no single source section — so it must not read as a dangling citation.
tests.key: computeBriefCoverage › ignores nodes with no sourceRef rather than counting them as dangling

tests.description: A heading with nothing under it is part of the document's shape, but there is nothing in it to have accounted for — counting it as untouched made the panel report one more unread section than the brief has.
tests.key: computeBriefCoverage › leaves an empty section out of both halves of the tally

tests.description: Silently dropping a citation would let `covered` overstate itself, which is the exact failure this feature exists to prevent.
tests.key: computeBriefCoverage › reports a node citing a section the brief does not have

tests.description: The untouched half is the valuable one, so it is a first-class output rather than something every caller has to filter for itself.
tests.key: computeBriefCoverage › reports untouched sections and how much document they are

tests.description: A map with no brief splits into no sections. Zeroed, not thrown: the workspace renders that state by mounting no panel at all.
tests.key: computeBriefCoverage › returns a zeroed coverage for a map with no brief

tests.description: A brief nobody has cited yet is the honest day-one picture, not an error.
tests.key: computeBriefCoverage › treats a brief with nothing cited as fully untouched

tests.description: An aligned pair should get a straight line, not a degenerate dog-leg with zero-length segments.
tests.key: connectorPath › drops straight down when parent and child share a centre

tests.description: Siblings share that bus, which is what makes the tree read as one structure rather than a set of unrelated lines.
tests.key: connectorPath › routes through a horizontal bus midway between the two levels

tests.description: A connector that started inside the parent pill or stopped short of the child would leave visible gaps against the dotted stroke.
tests.key: connectorPath › starts at the parent bottom edge and ends at the child top edge

tests.description: A second root would read as a second idea rather than a contribution to this one, so an unparented node hangs off the root.
tests.key: contributionEvents — adding a node › attaches to the root when no parent is named

tests.description: Without this the person's node would be logged as an intention and never appear on the map — the bug this module exists to fix.
tests.key: contributionEvents — adding a node › creates the node and logs it with the real id

tests.description: The kind comes from a picker over NODE_KINDS, but the route is reachable by anything; an unknown kind the map cannot draw must not reach the tree.
tests.key: contributionEvents — adding a node › falls back to a drawable kind when the requested one is not real

tests.description: The root fallback must not override a caller that knows where the node belongs — an answer elaborating on a question hangs under that question.
tests.key: contributionEvents — adding a node › honours an explicit parent

tests.description: `origin: user` is the same fact the pill reads to badge the node and the tools read to avoid re-ingesting their own writes, so the badge and the tool contract agree by construction.
tests.key: contributionEvents — adding a node › marks the node as the person’s

tests.description: Siblings are ordered, and a new one belongs after the ones already there.
tests.key: contributionEvents — adding a node › orders a new sibling after the existing ones

tests.description: An empty label would put an unreadable pill on the map, so nothing is written and nothing is logged.
tests.key: contributionEvents — adding a node › writes nothing for an empty label

tests.description: The answer is the person's act; closing the question is its consequence. Both must be logged, because an agent reading the log has to see that the map changed, not just that something was said.
tests.key: contributionEvents — answering › closes the answered question and logs both halves

tests.description: Answering twice must not invent a second change. The second answer is still worth logging — the person said something — but the node moved once.
tests.key: contributionEvents — answering › does not report a second close when the question is already answered

tests.description: A node the agent has since deleted must not fail the write. The answer itself is the part worth keeping.
tests.key: contributionEvents — answering › keeps the answer when the question node is gone

tests.description: The payload arrives from a browser and is untrusted on this side of the wire; a malformed one must degrade to "they said something", not throw.
tests.key: contributionEvents — answering › tolerates a malformed answers payload

tests.description: A note is something said ABOUT the map, not a change to it. Writing a node here would put the person's aside into the tree.
tests.key: contributionEvents — leaving a note › logs the note and changes nothing on the map

tests.description: The cheap cursor read the waiting tools report from.
tests.key: currentRevision › reports the map’s revision without reading the log

tests.description: A missing map must be an error rather than a zero, which a caller would mistake for a real cursor at the start of the log.
tests.key: currentRevision › throws for a map that does not exist

tests.description: SQLite has no JSON column, so payloads are strings that could be anything. A single unparseable row must not take down a whole catch-up read — the revision and kind are the load-bearing parts and they survive.
tests.key: decodeEvent › degrades to a null payload rather than throwing on bad JSON

tests.description: An empty column is the other shape a bad write leaves behind, and it must degrade identically rather than throwing.
tests.key: decodeEvent › handles an empty payload string the same way

tests.description: The happy path: SQLite hands back a string and the agent needs an object.
tests.key: decodeEvent › parses the stored payload back into an object

tests.description: Any heading level, and any leading blank space before it.
tests.key: deriveTitle › accepts a deeper heading level and leading blank lines

tests.description: A long heading is clipped with an ellipsis so the pill stays readable.
tests.key: deriveTitle › clips a long brief heading to 60 characters

tests.description: The same clipping rule as before, unchanged.
tests.key: deriveTitle › clips a long seed idea to 60 characters

tests.description: A brief with no headings still has a first line worth naming it after.
tests.key: deriveTitle › falls back to the first non-empty line of a headless brief

tests.description: A brief with nothing but blank lines cannot name anything, so the seed idea takes over rather than the map being titled an empty string.
tests.key: deriveTitle › falls back to the seed idea when the brief has no usable line

tests.description: A short seed idea is left exactly as it is.
tests.key: deriveTitle › leaves a short seed idea untouched

tests.description: A brief's own first heading is the document's title, and almost always right.
tests.key: deriveTitle › prefers the first markdown heading of a brief

tests.description: Without a brief this is the behaviour every existing map was named by, and it must not have changed.
tests.key: deriveTitle › uses the seed idea when there is no brief

tests.description: A note's whole value is its text, so it comes through as the note field the row renders with question emphasis.
tests.key: describeEvent › carries a note through as text

tests.description: The phase nav numbers its labels; a sentence should not.
tests.key: describeEvent › drops the phase number when reporting a phase change

tests.description: The label is denormalised at write time, so a question whose node was since deleted still reads as something rather than falling through to the raw kind name.
tests.key: describeEvent › falls back to naming no node when the label is gone

tests.description: A malformed payload must still produce a readable row: the rail is the person's only record, so degrading beats disappearing.
tests.key: describeEvent › falls back when the payload carries no label

tests.description: A user.node carries the created node's real label, and quoting it back is what confirms to the person that what they typed reached the map.
tests.key: describeEvent › names a node the person added

tests.description: Naming the node is the entire difference between a question and a note. A row reading "You asked a question" would put the reader back to guessing which of twenty pills it was about.
tests.key: describeEvent › names the node a question was about

tests.description: One answer can be shown; several cannot, because the row has no way to say which question each belongs to.
tests.key: describeEvent › shows the answer text only when a single question was answered

tests.description: "Agent asked 1 questions" is the kind of seam that makes a surface read as machine output rather than an account of what happened.
tests.key: describeEvent › singularises one question and counts several

tests.description: The entry keys off the LAST event so the revision is the cursor the run actually left the map at.
tests.key: describeRun › carries the last revision in the run

tests.description: Past one, the count IS the information — an agent turn that wrote four nodes is one act, and four near-identical rows would bury the rest of the log.
tests.key: describeRun › counts them once there is more than one

tests.description: Naming the thing beats counting it when there is only one.
tests.key: describeRun › names the node when the run is a single add

tests.description: The map is co-authored, so a row has to say WHICH side acted and whether something was created or changed — both halves of "who did what".
tests.key: describeRun › says "You" for the person and distinguishes an update

tests.description: Reserved for genuine faults: a conflict or a timeout is a normal result, and flagging those as errors would invite the blind retry the conflict path exists to prevent.

tests.description: Each of these is written somewhere in the spine and read back by an agent. One dropped from the list becomes a row nothing can resume past.

tests.description: A typo would become a row nothing knows how to render or resume from.

tests.description: An unknown or unreadable size must not, on its own, make an empty extraction look healthy. This is the half of the detached-buffer bug that IS decidable here: with a zero size the thin-text rule cannot fire, so the empty-text rule has to stand on its own. The other half — that the size is measured BEFORE extraction, since pdfjs transfers the buffer to its worker and detaches it — lives at the call site in briefText.ts and cannot be reached from a pure function. It was verified against the runnin

tests.key: timeoutMsFrom › caps a timeout longer than the ceiling

tests.description: Most agents will not pass one, so the default is the value that actually governs how long a person has to answer.
tests.key: timeoutMsFrom › falls back to the default when the agent names no timeout

tests.description: A zero or negative wait would make the tool a busy-loop rather than a wait.
tests.key: timeoutMsFrom › floors a zero or negative timeout at one second

tests.description: An agent that knows its own patience should get exactly what it asked for.
tests.key: timeoutMsFrom › uses the agent’s timeout when it is reasonable

tests.description: What a driver or a browser agent lists. It must match the catalog exactly, since a tool missing here is a tool the agent never knows it can call.
tests.key: toolSummaries › summarises every catalog tool with a name, title and description

tests.description: It asks for something rather than only reporting an absence — the point is to get the section dealt with on the agent's next turn.
tests.key: untouchedNoteText › asks the agent to act rather than only reporting the gap

tests.description: It names the section both ways: the mark the person just clicked, and the heading, so the agent can find it without another round trip.
tests.key: untouchedNoteText › names the section by mark and heading

tests.description: These three are what the contribution affordances post. Narrowing this set would silently drop a person's contribution on the floor.
tests.key: user-writable event kinds › accepts the three kinds a person can contribute

tests.description: The agent's own kinds are minted by the tools. Accepting one from the browser would let a page forge the other side of the conversation.
tests.key: user-writable event kinds › refuses the kinds only an agent may write

tests.description: A tool whose fields are all optional must accept an omitted payload rather than forcing the agent to send an empty object.
tests.key: validateToolInput › accepts a missing payload for a tool that needs no arguments

tests.description: The happy path returns the parsed input, so defaults and coercions the schema applies are what actually reach the server.
tests.key: validateToolInput › accepts input that fits the tool and hands back the parsed value

tests.description: The message has to name the offending field, or the agent can only guess at what to change.
tests.key: validateToolInput › names the field that did not fit

tests.description: A required field left out is the other common agent mistake.
tests.key: validateToolInput › rejects a call missing a required field

tests.description: The controlled vocabulary is what keeps the map drawable: a kind the map cannot render must never reach the database.
tests.key: validateToolInput › rejects a node kind the map cannot draw

tests.description: The phase drives the nav; one outside the loop would leave the workspace with no step marked active.
tests.key: validateToolInput › rejects a phase outside the loop

tests.description: A name the catalog does not know must come back as an answer, not a throw, or one bad call takes down the whole binding.
tests.key: validateToolInput › rejects a tool the catalog does not define

tests.description: Answering closes the question. Both halves are the same act, and the answer is the half worth a row.
tests.key: visibleEvents › hides the node.updated that an answer closed

tests.description: ask_user writes the question nodes AND announces them. Showing both would report one act twice, and the bare adds are the half nobody can act on.
tests.key: visibleEvents › hides the question nodes that a question.asked announced

tests.description: An open-question node put on the map WITHOUT an ask_user is a real contribution — nothing announced it, so nothing may hide it.
tests.key: visibleEvents › keeps a question node that nothing announced

tests.description: A user update that is not the answer's own close — a relabel, say — is a real edit and is not bookkeeping.
tests.key: visibleEvents › keeps a user update that is not the answer close

tests.description: The suppression is narrow on purpose: an AGENT closing the same node is a separate act by the other side and must still be reported.
tests.key: visibleEvents › keeps an agent update to a node the person answered

tests.description: Folding is depth-unbounded: a grandchild goes with its parent's branch.
tests.key: visibleNodes › drops descendants at every depth, not just direct children

tests.description: Two folded branches are independent of each other.
tests.key: visibleNodes › handles several collapsed branches at once

tests.description: An id that is not on the map must not disturb the result.
tests.key: visibleNodes › ignores a collapsed id that matches no node

tests.description: A leaf has nothing underneath, so folding it is a no-op rather than an error.
tests.key: visibleNodes › is a no-op for a node with no children

tests.description: The folded node itself stays — it is what you click to unfold again.
tests.key: visibleNodes › keeps the collapsed node and drops only what is under it

tests.description: Folding the root leaves the root alone on the map, not an empty map.
tests.key: visibleNodes › leaves just the root when the root is collapsed

tests.description: The map panel renders before any node exists, so folding must survive the day-one map rather than assuming there is a tree to walk.
tests.key: visibleNodes › returns an empty list for an empty map

tests.description: Nothing folded is the ordinary case and must not disturb the input.
tests.key: visibleNodes › returns every node when nothing is collapsed

tests.description: The layout guards against a parentId cycle so a malformed map still draws; folding has to survive the same input rather than spinning on it.
tests.key: visibleNodes › terminates on a parentId cycle

tests.description: The agent's own writes must not wake it — otherwise an agent that posts a note wakes itself and never actually waits for the person.
tests.key: waitForUserActivity › does not wake on the agent’s own writes

tests.description: An event may already be waiting. A waiter that subscribed before checking would sleep through it and time out with the answer already on disk.
tests.key: waitForUserActivity › returns immediately when the person already acted

tests.description: The timeout must RESOLVE, not hang and not throw. This is the guarantee an earlier unref'd-deadline bug broke: the promise simply never settled.
tests.key: waitForUserActivity › times out cleanly with a resume cursor when nobody acts

tests.description: The wake path: a user write during the wait must be delivered.
tests.key: waitForUserActivity › wakes and returns the user’s events when they act during the wait

tests.description: This is the string every codeyam preview and captured scenario shows. It has to read as an expected condition, not as a failure.
tests.key: webMcpUnavailableReason › names the iframe

tests.description: Each reason names a different fix, so they must not collapse into one generic "unavailable" the person cannot act on.
tests.key: webMcpUnavailableReason › names the insecure context

tests.description: Naming the version requirement is the difference between a person knowing what to do next and assuming the page is broken.
tests.key: webMcpUnavailableReason › names the missing browser agent

tests.description: A bound page must return null, since the UI shows this string only when there is genuinely something wrong to report.
tests.key: webMcpUnavailableReason › reports nothing to explain when the page is bound

tests.description: The security gates are checked before the agent gate, so an insecure page is told to fix that first rather than being sent hunting for a browser.
tests.key: webMcpUnavailableReason › reports the security problem first when several apply
